decision.protocol_pick: no model finished any of the five goals on screen (0 done everywhere), so the protocol's tie-breaks decide: fewest errors would be MiniMax (0 HTTP errors), but its runs were empty answers or the wrong tool (builtIn_emitSparkCommand), so that is not a usable pick.

what_the_runs_show.dahl GLM-5.3-Flash: the only model that used the right tool names and the new persona (jarvis_tasks, jarvis_recall, doc_reader); every failure was Dahl's own capacity limit (HTTP 429 model_concurrency: 'paid accounts are admitted first'), 24 of them, and one run took 7 rounds; 70-170 s per goal
what_the_runs_show.dahl MiniMax-M2.7: no HTTP errors, 30-110 s, but empty replies or builtIn_emitSparkCommand (a spark-command tool that is not the task) on 7 of 7 runs
what_the_runs_show.groq gpt-oss-120b: HTTP 413 on every goal: the face's request is 40 KB (about 10,000 tokens) and Groq's free tier takes 8,000 in all; it stays the private lane's model for the small Hermes prompt
what_the_runs_show.local: Ling-heretic and Granite abliterated are not installed

decision.provider_order: unchanged: dahl first (the face's model, GLM-5.3-Flash), then the fallbacks in the gateway order, local last. MiniMax is not set first because it did not use tools in the face.
followups: the face sends a second request of 8 KB next to every turn; with Dahl's concurrency cap it doubles the 429s
a model that follows the tool list in the face is the open problem: try Cerebras once its key exists (room for the 40 KB request: 30K tokens a minute)
